The engine as it stands: 10x12 mailbox board, attack maps, full legal move generation with castling/en-passant/promotions, PVS with killer-move ordering, quiescence over captures and promotions, material + piece-square evaluation, iterative deepening to a fixed node budget (deterministic, no clock). messages.content: Edited engine2.py: break added after the snapshot restore.

Third grade: elo 708, one repetition draw vs depth-2, five checkmate losses. Direct tactical tests found the decisive bug: in make() the capture delta had the sign inverted (score -= the captured piece's value), so the search valued every capture as a loss — it ignored free queens and gave material away. Flipping the sign.
Capture score delta corrected for en passant and normal captures.
Edited engine2.py: en-passant capture sign fixed.
Same fix for normal captures.
Edited engine2.py: normal-capture sign fixed.

After the sign fix the engine mates a greedy material-capturer with both colours and finds mate-in-1s; perft still exact. Fourth grade: elo 708 again, 5 checkmate losses, trial 543 s, replay matched byte for byte (deterministic). The house engines extend every reply to a check; ours had no check handling at all (quiescence stood pat in check). Adding check extension in the main search and full evasion search with mate/stalemate detection in quiescence.
Quiescence rewritten: no stand-pat in check; when in check it searches every evasion and returns -MATE+ply when mated, 0 when stalemated.

    global NODES

    ks=P.wk if P.stm>0 else P.bk
    ick=attacked(P,ks,P.stm<0)

Committed as 297878ac8eff333814351486bbb519d69e00335f and pushed to github.com/SufTTY/tiny-chess-01 (master and main; default branch main). Local grades confirm: no time losses, replay byte for byte identical, exit code 0, main.py 3747 bytes, repository total 6599 bytes. Honest status: still below the house baseline locally (~700 Elo vs the 1154 floor); known gaps: no transposition table, no repetition/50-move scoring inside the search, material+PST-only eval. Submitting as the slot-1 probe to pass intake and read the leaderboard; slots 2-3 iterate on TT and repetition scores.
Upgrade the kept tiny-chess-01 entry (strongest 4KB Python chess engine, rank by elo) and re-submit. Slug: tiny-chess-01.

Fetched the leaderboard: everyone who wins all games is pinned at elo 2110, so the tie-break spare_plies decides ranks; our kept entry (01a1e736) shows 2110 with 991 spare plies and rank 1 has 1082. Plan: raise search depth per move without risking the 1800s trial wall clock. Tested three candidates against engine2 with a fixed-depth node-count bench on 4 positions (kiwipete, WAC puzzle, rook endgame, start): (1) transposition table with per-node hash of the 120-square board - a clear net loss, hashing costs more than TT saves at these depths; rejected. (2) null-move pruning (R=2, d>=3, non-pawn material guard) plus history heuristic - measurably worse, e.g. 862k nodes vs 511k at depth 4 on the WAC puzzle; rejected. (3) adaptive per-move node budget: keep the proven 80k PVS+quiescence core but run 110k nodes/move while trial elapsed < 700s, 80k to 1200s, then throttle to 40k so the whole trial can never hit the wall. Chose (3): strictly deeper search early when time is plentiful, bounded late-game cost, no new per-node overhead. Verified move generation still correct via perft (Kiwipete: 48/2039/97862).
